method: Signal is measured out of sample from data/verified/backtest.json and involves no money. Staking and masking are binomial samplings with a fixed seed, so every number is reproducible by re-running the script. No market price exists in the repository.

signal.what_this_proves: On 89 games the model never saw, it beats predicting a zero margin on MAE (9.29 vs 10.21 points) and gets the winner's side of the final score 56 of 88 times (p=0.0138). The pipeline carries real information about the score.
signal.what_this_does_not_prove: It is NOT an edge over a market. A closing line is far better than predict-zero, and this repository has no prices, so the only comparison that would matter has not been made. Sign accuracy against the final score is not a win rate at a price, and no bankroll, ROI or reward may be derived from it.

masking.a_reading: A strategy whose TRUE win rate is 45% - far below the 52.4% breakeven - still finishes above its starting bankroll 6.6% of the time after 100 bets. A bankroll column is therefore not evidence of skill and cannot be a ranking key.
masking.b_reading: With only 20 bets, a strategy whose true rate is 47% finishes ahead of one whose true rate is 55% 25.3% of the time. At 200 bets that falls to 5.0%. A leaderboard read at a short sample is mostly noise.
masking.c_reading: At -110, a true 55% bettor needs about 2272 settled bets before a one-sided exact binomial test rejects breakeven 80% of the time. That is the arithmetic behind the minimum-sample gate, not a preference.

limits: One season. The signal itself has a wide interval; 137 games cannot establish a durable edge.
Independent identically distributed bets are assumed, which understates real slate variance where same-week bets are correlated.
No commission, limit, line movement or push handling is modelled.
The staking block illustrates variance; it is not a performance record and must never be quoted as an ROI.
